name: Laos

facts.religion: Theravada Buddhism about 65%, animist and other

snapshot: A one-party communist state heavily in debt to China, whose 2026 party congress and assembly vote kept the same leadership in place.
culture: Laos is deeply Buddhist; in Luang Prabang, saffron-robed monks collect alms at dawn. Sticky rice is eaten with the hands at almost every meal. The khaen, a bamboo mouth organ, is central to Lao music. Boun Pi Mai, the new year in April, is celebrated with water fights.
society: The US dropped more bombs on Laos during the Vietnam War than on Germany and Japan in the Second World War, and unexploded ordnance still kills people. A Chinese-built railway opened in 2021, but debt to China is huge and inflation and currency collapse have hit households. Dams on the Mekong make Laos a power exporter.
situation: The ruling Lao People's Revolutionary Party held its 12th congress in January 2026, and the new National Assembly re-elected Thongloun Sisoulith as president in March, along with Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone.
power: A one-party communist state. The Lao People's Revolutionary Party's Politburo makes the key decisions; the National Assembly elects the president, who also leads the party, and approves the prime minister.

leaders.state: President Thongloun Sisoulith, also party general secretary
